subject: Post-demo: hosting profile, migration constraints & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@NimbusPay.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: hosting profile, migration constraints & next steps

Hi Sanjay — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and a few asks so we can scope the POC and procurement path:

Call highlights (short):
- Primary hosting options under consideration: Hosted API (fast ramp), Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs), Private VPC / on-prem (SOC2 + data residency).
- Current environment: you mentioned a legacy GPU cluster in a colo with an existing non-Redwood self-hosted LLM stack; you're also running some traffic through a public LLM API for edge use cases.
- Major constraints: SOC2 controls, no outbound model data to third-party clouds for certain flows, predictable throughput for peak batch scoring.

Asks / next steps:
1) Confirm preferred hosting mode(s) to prioritize in the POC: Hosted | Dedicated | Private (we can run a multi-mode proof if you want to compare).
2) Share a short procurement timeline (procurement lead + target PO/contract date).
3) Provide baseline perf targets: tokens/sec at 32k context, typical queries/sec (p95) and KV cache hit expectations.
4) Do you need on-prem installer or is VPC-only acceptable for now?

I can loop in Monica (solutions) and Karthik (inference infra) for a technical deep-dive once we get the perf numbers and procurement window. I attached a hosted vs dedicated vs private comparison workbook and a sample SOW outline to start procurement.

Proposed immediate next step: a 30–45m infra deep-dive on Thu or Fri this week to settle the POC scope. Let me know which day/time works.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-hosting-comparison.xlsx (workbook summary), SOW-draft-NimbusPay-v1.docx (SOW template)
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@NimbusPay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Menon <priya.menon@nimbuspay.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: hosting profile, migration constraints & next steps

Marissa — great summary, thanks. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Hosting preference: We want to evaluate Dedicated capacity first (predictable latency and isolation), with Private VPC as a hard requirement for any PII or payment flow. Hosted API is attractive for prototyping but will not be acceptable for cardholder-data-related endpoints due to compliance.

2) Current stack: we are running an older Llama-based self-hosted model on a 4-node GPU cluster in our colo (on-prem-ish). Cost and scaling are the pain points — we also have some volume on a general-purpose public LLM API for low-sensitivity features. We're looking to lift-and-shift scoring to a managed dedicated pool if performance is equal or better and cost predictable.

3) Performance targets: baseline production p95 latency target ~250ms for 512-token generation, concurrency ~160 qps for high-traffic windows (batch scoring spikes up to 1,000 qps for small requests), typical seq lengths 64–512 tokens.

4) Procurement timeline: procurement lead is Priya Menon; target to have contracts signed by end of Q3 (Sept 30). Priya attached our procurement timeline and vendor checklist. 

We are open to starting a limited POC in July for functional validation, then a technical perf POC in August. Can do the deep-dive Thursday 17 Jun 10:30am PT.

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Head of ML Platform, NimbusPay
Sanjay.Rao@NimbusPay.com

Attachments: nimbus-procurement-timeline.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@NimbusPay.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: hosting profile, migration constraints & next steps

Perfect — thanks for the detail, Sanjay. Confirming Thu 17 Jun 10:30am PT for the infra deep-dive. 

What we'll cover in the deep-dive:
- POC goals (functional vs perf split) and acceptance criteria
- Migration paths: (A) Direct lift from your colo cluster to Redwood Dedicated (image/weights transfer + kv cache migration), (B) Hybrid: Private VPC for sensitive flows + Hosted for low-sensitivity features, (C) Plugin to keep some fast path on your legacy cluster while offloading batch scoring to Redwood.
- Security controls: KMS/HSM options, audit log export, and ingress/egress controls for Private deployments.
- Success metrics and telemetry hooks we need from your infra.

Action items for you before Thu: share the perf baselines you mentioned (p95 target numbers + sample traffic CSV), and Priya's preferred contract timeline. Monica — can you prepare a short checklist for data residency/procurement questions (SOC2 evidence, network diagrams, egress policy)? Karthik — please prep an estimate for a two-month Dedicated POC and a short note on model/weights transfer constraints.

I'll draft a brief agenda and send calendar invite.

Best,
Marissa

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@NimbusPay.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Technical notes: throughput assumptions and POC blueprint

Sanjay / Marissa — quick technical note ahead of today's call: 

1) For the Dedicated POC we typically size to steady-state qps and then validate burst capacity; given Sanjay's numbers (160 qps steady, spikes to 1k qps for small requests) we will propose a dual-pool approach: a smaller low-latency pool optimized for 512-token generation and a separate batch pool for high-concurrency scoring.

2) Model migration: if you provide model checkpoints + containerized runtime we can do an in-place compatibility check. If transfer of weights is restricted, we can run test harnesses against a mirrored dataset. We should confirm whether the current weights are quantized and which framework (PyTorch / ONNX).

3) KV caching: expectation on hit rate will materially change cost; please share sample hit-rate targets if available.

4) Private VPC: we need a network contact to exchange allowed CIDR ranges and VPN/Direct Connect details.

I'll include a short sizing worksheet in the post-call notes. Looking forward to the call.

Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@NimbusPay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Menon <priya.menon@nimbuspay.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: hosting profile, migration constraints & next steps

Thanks all — the call was helpful. A few concrete commitments and clarifications: 

- We will proceed with a 2-month Dedicated POC (functional + perf) starting 02 Aug 2027. Procurement will aim to complete PO and NDAs by 31 Jul. Priya will lead procurement and send a DocuSign envelope for standard terms next week.

- For the POC we will provide: a sanitized subset of scoring requests (CSV), sample model checkpoint (if allowed), and an infra contact for VPC peering. If weight transfer is restricted we authorize a mirrored test harness instead.

- Priorities: match p95 latency <=250ms for 512 tokens; validate batch pool throughput to handle 1k qps small-requests burst with acceptable queueing.

Forwarding Priya's procurement notes below.
